The repair.py half is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: the placeholder blanker at reckon/crew/node.py:136 blanks only double quotes and backticks, so the single-quoted `<id>` placeholders the composer used to write would be read as an unresolved placeholder and refused by validate_node (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3377), and negative_control_finding (reckon/crew/node.py:892, applied at dispatch.py:3385) refuses a composed node whose scope names test files with no negative_control declared.
item_verdicts.done_when: The done-when is the focused file plus the arm comparison; I re-ran the focused file in the reviewed worktree at db89a867d (tests/test_reflex_dispatches_one_repair.py, 14 passed in 30.87s, EXIT=0) and re-derived both arms' failure-id sets from their own logs: head ids are a strict subset of base ids, so added is 0, and the head population is exactly the 102 tests/ files my independent AST scan finds importing reckon.crew.recovery or reckon.crew.repair.
item_verdicts.goal: The goal is one composed repair node per finding-bearing implement review round, and dispatch_repair_for_run (reckon/crew/recovery.py:1551) delivers it: tests/test_reflex_dispatches_one_repair.py:285 drives a real sweep over a stored three-finding review and observes exactly one repair whose brief names all three content-derived ids, which I reproduced (14 passed, EXIT=0), with the recorded narrowing that a round whose findings cite only run records dispatches nothing (reckon/crew/recovery.py:1418).
item_verdicts.manifest: Read in full; both suite records' failure ids match the logs exactly (32 base ids, 31 head ids, set-equal), its added-failure claim re-derives to zero through the store's own reader, and its two evidence shortfalls are the base log header and the unterminated negative-control log named in the findings below.
item_verdicts.write_paths: The manifest declares five orientation_write_paths and `git diff --name-status 25dabb312 db89a867d` lists four files, every one inside that set (reckon/crew/recovery.py, reckon/crew/repair.py, tests/test_reflex_dispatches_one_repair.py, docs/evidence/fragments/a-review-is-sized-to-its-risk/reflex-repairs-only-idle-implement-runs.html); the declared docs/figures/ path is unused, and a fence is not a quota.

justifications.durability: Each guard names the condition that reddens it — removing the live-or-resumed check reddens tests/test_reflex_dispatches_one_repair.py:394, as negative-control.log demonstrates — but the worker-record liveness branch (reckon/crew/recovery.py:1386) and the died-without-ledger redispatch branch of _repair_in_flight (recovery.py:1520) carry no test.
justifications.evidence: The focused gate reproduces (14 passed, EXIT=0) and the store's own reader derives 0 added failures with both arms' id lists matching the manifest exactly, but the base arm's header asserts the wrong module under test (/home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20260929T194125547716-reflex-repairs-only-idle-implement-runs/arm-base.log:3) and the declared negative-control log lacks its EXIT= terminator (/home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20260929T194125547716-reflex-repairs-only-idle-implement-runs/negative-control.log:27).
justifications.fit: The report-and-return idiom matches dispatch_review_for_run beside it (reckon/crew/recovery.py:1128), the new names are mechanism-named (REPAIR_DISPATCH_FIELD, _repairable_scope, REPAIR_NODE_PREFIX), and the source carries no plan, ticket or role-attribution string.
justifications.goal_fidelity: recovery.py:1551 composes through repair.py:259 and the sweep dispatches it at recovery.py:1925, which is the goal's sentence; the record-only refusal at recovery.py:1418 is a deliberate, disclosed narrowing of "the union of the paths the findings name" beyond what the plan's §3 words require.
justifications.scope_discipline: `git diff --name-status 25dabb312 db89a867d` lists only the four declared paths, and both supporting fixes are implied by the composed node having to validate at dispatch (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3377).
